goeppertia-allouia.name: Lerén
goeppertia-allouia.summary: A plant native to northern South America and the Caribbean, also called Guinea arrowroot, and one of the earliest crops domesticated by prehistoric Amerindians.

s-o-raimundo-nonato.name: São Raimundo Nonato
s-o-raimundo-nonato.summary: A city in southern Piauí, Brazil, about 576 km from the capital Teresina, known as the location of the Serra da Capivara National Park.

santar-m-par.name: Santarém
santar-m-par.summary: A city in the western Brazilian Amazon at the meeting of the Tapajós and Amazon rivers, founded by Portuguese colonists in 1661 and once home to the Tapajós people.

piau.name: Piauí
piau.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil with the shortest coastline of any coastal Brazilian state, colonized inland before the coast, and home to the rock-art-rich Serra da Capivara National Park.

rio-grande-do-norte.name: Rio Grande do Norte
rio-grande-do-norte.summary: A Brazilian state at the country's northeasternmost tip, with its capital at Natal and an economy based on tourism, oil extraction and agriculture.

arrowroot.name: Arrowroot
arrowroot.summary: A starch obtained from the rhizomes of tropical plants, traditionally Maranta arundinacea, though the name is used for several similar starches.

santa-catarina-state.name: Santa Catarina
santa-catarina-state.summary: A state in southern Brazil on the Atlantic coast, known for its mountainous terrain, with Florianópolis as its capital.

rio-grande-do-sul.name: Rio Grande do Sul
rio-grande-do-sul.summary: A southern Brazilian state bordering Uruguay and Argentina, with capital Porto Alegre, shaped by Guarani and Kaingang peoples, Jesuit and Azorean settlers, and German and Italian migration.

caverna-da-pedra-pintada.name: Caverna da Pedra Pintada
caverna-da-pedra-pintada.summary: An archaeological cave site in northern Brazil showing evidence of human presence from about 11,200 years ago, which challenged earlier ideas about South American settlement patterns.

tembet.name: Tembetá
tembet.summary: A metal or stone rod worn in a lower-lip piercing by some indigenous South American peoples since the Neolithic, marking body modification, spiritual protection, or sexual maturity.

brazilian-highlands.name: Brazilian Highlands
brazilian-highlands.summary: An extensive plateau covering about half of Brazil's land area, home to most of the country's population, shaped by ancient lava flows and erosion.

pedra-furada.name: Pedra Furada
pedra-furada.summary: An archaeological complex of over 800 sites in Piauí, Brazil, with rock paintings around 12,000 years old and possible human traces from 48,000 to 32,000 years ago; a World Heritage Site since 1991.

tapaj-people.name: Santarém culture
tapaj-people.summary: Pottery tradition of the Tapajós, an Indigenous Brazilian people who lived where the Tapajós River meets the Amazon; studied by anthropologist Helen Palmatary in the 1930s.

chicha.name: Chicha
chicha.summary: A traditional Andean and Amazonian beverage, most commonly a corn beer called chicha de jora, used ceremonially in the Inca Empire.
